project: Terrain Elevate P1 Stair-Climbing Stroller Mechanism

locked_constraints.truth_boundary: Mechanism CAD generation only. No native FEA, certification, or physical verification claimed.

geometry.stair_reference_reason: 203.2 mm rise x 279.4 mm going is exactly 8.00 in x 11.00 in. DELIBERATELY BEYOND CODE, not a code figure: IRC 2021 R311.7.5.1 caps residential riser height at 7-3/4 in (196.85 mm) and requires a minimum 10 in (254 mm) tread depth, and IBC is stricter still at 7 in for most commercial stairs. The reference is set one quarter-inch above the residential maximum because the vehicle must work on real existing staircases, including older and non-conforming ones built before or outside current code, not only on compliant new construction. Designing to the code maximum exactly would leave zero margin on the very stairs most likely to need a stair-climbing stroller.
geometry.stair_reference_consequence: This choice sets the wheel diameter, which is the single most visually dominant dimension on the vehicle. The unaided-nosing-rollover rule requires wheel radius >= stair rise, so 203.2 mm rise forces a minimum 406.4 mm wheel; the selected 430 mm carries 11.8 mm of margin over that floor. At the IRC residential maximum of 196.85 mm the floor would instead be 393.7 mm, so honouring code exactly rather than exceeding it would save only about 13 mm of wheel diameter -- the wheel is large because of the rollover rule itself, not because of this margin. For scale, a mainstream jogging stroller (BOB Revolution Flex) already runs 16 in / 406 mm rear wheels.
geometry.stair_reference_source_SRC: IRC 2021 R311.7.5.1 (max riser 7-3/4 in) and R311.7.5.2 (min tread 10 in), International Code Council.
